verses.pali: Assuttha no tumhe, bhikkhave, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ jarasiṅgālassa vassamānassā”ti?
verses.english: Mendicants, did you hear an old jackal howling at the crack of dawn?”

verses.pali: “Eso kho, bhikkhave, jarasiṅgālo ukkaṇḍakena nāma rogajātena phuṭṭho neva bilagato ramati, na rukkhamūlagato ramati, na ajjhokāsagato ramati;
verses.english: “That old jackal has the disease called mange. He’s not happy in his den, or at the root of a tree, or out in the open.

verses.pali: yena yena gacchati, yattha yattha tiṭṭhati, yattha yattha nisīdati, yattha yattha nipajjati; tattha tattha anayabyasanaṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: Wherever he goes, stands, sits, or lies down he meets with tragedy and disaster.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhikkhu lābhasakkārasilokena abhibhūto pariyādiṇṇacitto neva suññāgāragato ramati, na rukkhamūlagato ramati, na ajjhokāsagato ramati;
verses.english: In the same way, take a certain mendicant whose mind is overcome and overwhelmed by possessions, honor, and popularity. They’re not happy in an empty hut, at the root of a tree, or out in the open.

verses.pali: yena yena gacchati, yattha yattha tiṭṭhati, yattha yattha nisīdati, yattha yattha nipajjati; tattha tattha anayabyasanaṁ āpajjati.
verses.english: Wherever they go, stand, sit, or lie down they meet with tragedy and disaster.
So grim are possessions, honor, and popularity. …”
